user.title: SunSprout Monitor
user.description: Pack temperatures the monitor treats as safe to charge in, by cell family. Look them up on your cell's data sheet. A board is matched by its Cell Chemistry or, for a custom chemistry, by the gauge's chemistry ID; other chemistries are not checked. Charging outside the window, or any time above 60 °C, raises a Repairs issue.

battery_values.title: Set up the battery
battery_values.description: Enter the details of the pack connected to {device}. Nothing is written until you confirm. Charging stays off until you turn it on.

data_description.chemistry: The chemistry of the pack. Li-ion raises the charge limit to 4.2 V; LiFePO4 charges to 3.65 V.
data_description.capacity_mah: The pack's rated capacity. The charger ends the charge at C/10 of this.
data_description.energy_mwh: Capacity times the nominal cell voltage. Leave 0 to have it worked out.
data_description.charge_current_ma: Used at every boot. 100 to 2000 mA; the board's copper is rated for 2 A.
data_description.thermistors: Which of the charger's (J302) and the fuel gauge's (J401) thermistors are fitted. A missing one makes the charger refuse to charge unless it is set to ignore it.
data_description.max_charge_temperature_c: The cell's highest charging temperature, from its data sheet (30 to 53 °C). Charging stops there and resumes 2 °C lower. 0 uses 45 °C.
data_description.termination_current_ma: The current the charge ends at (40 to 1000 mA, in steps of 40). 0 is automatic: 40 mA for LiFePO4, C/10 for Li-ion. The fuel gauge's taper current follows it.
data_description.cell_charge_voltage: The most each cell is charged to, per cell. 0 uses the standard for the chemistry (3.65 V LiFePO4, 4.20 V Li-ion). Set a lower one if the cell's data sheet gives it (for example 3.60 V); lower is always the safe direction. It can never be higher than the standard.

battery_confirm.title: Confirm the battery setup

battery_done.title: Battery setup recorded
battery_done.description:
{device} now remembers that its setup is done, even if this integration is removed.

Next: load the fuel gauge's chemistry table if you have not, run the gauge calibrations, enable Impedance Track, then run a full charge and discharge so the gauge can learn the pack. Turn Enable Charging on when you are ready.

satellites.title: Satellite addresses
satellites.description:
Choose the I2C addresses each satellite on {device} uses. They must match the jumpers on the satellite: the ADS1115 (soil moisture) address comes from its ADDR pin and the DS2482 (soil temperature) address from AD0 and AD1. Two satellites cannot share an address.
{satellites}{scan_note}

satellites_applied.title: Power cycle to apply
satellites_applied.description: {device} reads the addresses when it starts, so a change only takes effect after the next boot. Power cycling the board now applies it at once and the board is off for about ten seconds.

satellites_done.title: Satellite addresses saved
satellites_done.description: {device} will use these addresses after its next boot.

error.termination_invalid: The termination current has to be 0 (automatic) or 40 to 1000 mA in steps of 40.

error.address_duplicate: Another satellite already uses this address.
error.voltage_invalid: The charge voltage has to be 0 (the standard) or between 3.35 V and the standard for the chemistry, and never above it.
